item.title: Choice principles in countable partition models
item.description: arXiv:2610.29752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the countable partition model over a set of atoms of arbitrary uncountable cardinality $\kappa$. Its supports are partitions of the atoms into countably many blocks, and a permutation fixes a support when it preserves each block setwise. This model was proposed by Bruce and studied by Banerjee. We prove that dependent choice holds for every $\kappa$, although the filter of subgroups is not closed under countable intersections. Choice for well-orderable families holds exactly when $\kappa<\aleph_{\omega_1}$; when $\kappa\ge\aleph_{\omega_1}$, an $\omega_1$-indexed family witnesses its failure. The Hartogs and Lindenbaum numbers of the set of atoms are both $\omega_1$. The proofs use permutations matching blocks of equal cardinality and establish shift completeness of the filter. Together with Banerjee's failure of $\mathsf{DC}_{\omega_1}$, these results determine which dependent choice principles hold in the model.
item.dc:creator: Brinda Venkataramani

item.title: General Criterion for a Poset to Admit a Partition Into $\omega$-Chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.29056v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given a poset $P$ with no maximal element the question naturally arises of when $P$ can be partitioned into $\omega$-chains. In this paper we give general criterion for when this can be done. We show that in the case when a poset with no maximal element is countable or a well-founded forest, then it can always be partitioned into $\omega$-chains. We then introduce the lifting property for posets with no maximal element and show that a poset can be partitioned into $\omega$-chains if and only if it has the lifting property.
item.dc:creator: Remi Salinas Schmeis

item.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.29211v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that for every open $ U \subseteq \mathbb R^n $ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb R$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We apply our theorem to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).
item.dc:creator: Thang Do, Arnulf Jentzen, Benno Kuckuck

item.title: Logic vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.29771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies doctrines in categorical logic and their relations to fragments of geometric logic. After a brief account of the historical context for the notion of doctrine in categorical logic, we propose our working definition. We then show that there is a Galois connection between the poset of doctrines and the poset of fragments of geometric logic as defined in the framework of Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi, recently developed by the first and third authors. Concretely, the connection is realised by a general construction of syntactic categories and classifying topoi which encompasses all well-known examples in categorical logic. This yields a mirror symmetry, between the algebraic world of doctrines and the geometric world of topoi: to provide evidence of this phenomenon, we prove a few symmetric results relating doctrines and logics by means of syntactic categories and classifying topoi. We conclude with a discussion on the theme of conceptual completeness.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Di Liberti, Umberto Tarantino, Lingyuan Ye

item.title: Classification of bipartite observables III: simplicity, mixtures and quantum error correction
item.description: arXiv:2610.22205v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This is the third of a series of three papers that bring model theory to quantum information. The dividing lines of Shelah's classification theory, which separate the tame first-order theories from the wild ones, become properties of bipartite observables: properties of the expectation values obtained when two independently prepared quantum systems are idealized one after the other. In this paper we focus on simple unstable theories. The Pauli group of quantum error correction, with anticommutation as its relation, has a simple unstable theory, like the random graph. Forking and the Kim--Pillay independence theorem acquire a meaning in stabilizer codes: forking recognizes logical errors, and the independence theorem glues syndromes.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Due\~{n}ez, Jos\'{e} Iovino

item.title: On stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a general decomposition for regular closed semilinear sets, derived from a detailed study of their topological boundary. As an application, we characterize stable semilinear sets in ordered vector spaces over an ordered field, extending previous results of Hoffmann, Tran, and Ye.
item.dc:creator: Marcos Gir\'on
